title: Hippocratic prognosis constructor with cause and time scope
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A complete Hippocratic Prognostic passage keeps one observed facial appearance while changing its prognostic consequence according to an explicitly queried prior cause and a day-and-night interval. Known component order supplies observation and query frames, the whole residual selects explained versus unexplained scope, and entry context selects onset versus later disease stage. This is a finite semantic contract, not a target gloss or medical claim.

source.work: Hippocratic Prognostic, Part 2, complete bounded passage
source.witness: Francis Adams English translation tradition, institutional MIT digital text; no Greek manuscript or medieval Latin witness is claimed.
source.historical_limit: The host conventionally dates the work around 400 BCE, but precise authorship/date and the exact print exemplar are unresolved in the packet. Historical prognoses are source assertions, not present medical advice.

composition_contract.known_parts: An ordered part frame creates OBSERVE(feature, site, baseline) and ASK(cause) argument slots; no part receives an English lexeme.
composition_contract.whole_residual: The complete residual selects SAME_APPEARANCE, CAUSE_QUERY, EXPLAINED, PERSISTENT, or PROGNOSIS rather than serving as an arbitrary symptom name.
composition_contract.entry_context: Context carries the same patient and observed appearance while distinguishing disease ONSET from DAY3_OR4 review and distinguishes the patient's own healthy baseline from comparison with other healthy people.
composition_contract.scope_rule: A confessed cause lowers danger for the observed appearance; it does not assert survival. Missing cause plus persistence after the written interval enters the severe branch.

complete_source_plan: H01: examine the countenance first; compare it with healthy people and more strongly with the patient's own healthy appearance.
H02: retain every adverse face/eye/ear/temple/forehead/color feature as one appearance bundle, not one guessed target noun per feature.
H03: at onset, if the appearance is not otherwise accounted for, ask about prolonged sleeplessness, loose bowels and lack of food.
H04: admission of any such cause lowers danger; preserve the day-and-night clarification interval without turning it into a cure.
H05: retain both later conditions and their unresolved connective scope: none of the causes reported, and symptoms not subsiding in the stated interval.
H06: at the third or fourth day, repeat the earlier inquiry and add signs on face, body and eyes.
H07-H10: retain all later eye, eyelid, lip and nose signs, their source severity distinctions, the sleep-eye exclusions, and the final mortal-lips assertion.
constructor.worked_trace: OBSERVE(A,FACE_BUNDLE,COUNTENANCE,ONSET) ; ASK(A,[SLEEP,BOWELS,FOOD]) ; EXPLAINED_BY(FACE_BUNDLE,SLEEP) ; WAIT(FACE_BUNDLE,DAY_AND_NIGHT) -> REDUCED_DANGER. Rival branch: UNEXPLAINED_AND_PERSISTENT(FACE_BUNDLE,DAY_AND_NIGHT) -> IMMINENT_DEATH_PROGNOSIS.
constructor.consequence: The same appearance has different source-prescribed outcomes depending on whether the queried antecedent is admitted and whether it persists after the interval. A complete writer must preserve the inquiry and time scope rather than assigning one fixed prognosis to the appearance.
constructor.rival: R-SIGN-DICTIONARY maps the appearance directly to one fatal or nonfatal outcome; R-CAUSE-ERASES treats an admitted cause as proof of safety. Both lose the source's reduced-danger qualification, interval check, and later repeat inquiry.
constructor.falsifier: Reject if a complete source-equivalent account allows the same appearance to receive its severe branch without the written absence/persistence conditions, if the cause query changes the patient identity, or if the later DAY3_OR4 clause cannot repeat the same inquiry frame while adding new signs. A target application would fail if components/context cannot expose observation, cause, scope and time as distinct roles.

predecessors.limit: Opinion/acceptance changes a contribution claim; this card instead tests one observed sign under cause and time conditions.
Conditional treatment has an ordered opposite-treatment sequence; this card has diagnostic inquiry and prognostic scope, not treatment.
Shared relation signatures delay lexical values; this card supplies a concrete observation/query/prognosis operator family and a severity rival.
Directed composition and whole residual are formal observations only; they motivate the contract but do not identify target roles.

dependencies: The two later if-clauses and the sleep-eye and purgation exclusions retain their source ambiguity; no Boolean repair is fitted.
Patient identity is account-local; repeated pronouns do not prove one historical patient across separate source cases.
No source medical claim is promoted to modern efficacy or target meaning.
No target data, reserve, image, decoder, experiment, route, ledger, or root file was accessed or changed.
